title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-noah-anderson
content:
Notes / scratchpad — redlines & negotiation points (working doc)

Context:
- Customer: Large SaaS customer (H). Evaluating Dedicated deployment + Private options; wants broad indemnities, data use for model improvement, long retention.
- Current sales ask: mutual SaaS + inference INFs + training rights. They gave a redline with unlimited liability carveouts and 90 day breach cure.

Priority clauses to watch (top of mind):
1) Liability cap
   - Typical redline: unlimited/wide exceptions.
   - Target: cap at lesser of (12 months of fees) or $X (discuss with finance).
   - Carve-outs: gross negligence, willful misconduct — keep carve-outs but try to limit to direct damages plus reasonable defense costs.
   - Push back on punitive/indirect exception.

2) Indemnity
   - Third-party IP claims: standard defend & indemnify for infringement alleging use as permitted by agreement.
   - Avoid customer-demanded indemnity for outputs of models that contain third-party content unless clear scope.
   - Seek mutual indemnities where appropriate (data breaches, IP).

3) Data use / model training / outputs
   - Customer wants Redwood to be able to use anonymized logs for model improvement.
   - For Private deployments we should restrict training/use of customer data.
   - Propose: "No training on Customer Data without explicit opt-in; can use aggregated/derived telemetry that is non-identifiable."
   - Add explicit prohibition on using PII or Customer Confidential Information for model training.

4) Confidentiality & exceptions
   - Standard confidentiality with 3-5 year survival.
   - Add explicit security incident notification timeline (48-72 hours initial notice + regular updates).

5) Security / SOC2 / audits
   - Customer asking for right-to-audit and penetration test results.
   - For Hosted: offer SOC2 Type II report and security questionnaire; limited right-to-audit via third-party auditor and redacted report.
   - For Private/on-prem: more flexibility — may negotiate on-site audit with notice and scope limits.

6) Subprocessors / subprocessors list
   - Ensure subprocessors clause requires notice + objection window; for Dedicated/Private, limit to approved cloud infra partners.

7) SLA / credits / remedies
   - Customers push for service credits and broad remedies. Keep remedies to credits and termination for material breach only.
   - Define clear SLOs (p50/p95 latency) and credits calculation. Add exclusions (force majeure, customer-caused issues, scheduled maintenance).

8) Export controls / compliance
   - Add representation that Customer will not use service for sanctioned activities. Align with export control language.

9) Termination / data return & deletion
   - On termination: return or delete Customer Data within 30 days; allow short archival hold for legal/regulatory holds but with time limit (e.g., 90 days).

10) IP / model outputs ownership
   - Customer ownership over their input data and output results. Redwood owns the service and underlying model weights and improvements unless explicitly contracted.
   - If customer pays for dedicated/private with terms guaranteeing models will not be used to train public models, reflect that in Data Use clause.

Quick negotiation scripts / talking points for AE/Legal call:
- "We can agree to use telemetry for product improvement, but we can't train on raw customer data without explicit opt-in; we can commit to anonymization and aggregation."
- "Liability cap tied to fees is standard; can discuss increasing cap for higher commitment levels but unlimited liability isn't acceptable."
- "For security audits we can provide SOC2 Type II and a 3rd-party audit path; on-site audits can be discussed for Private deployments under narrow scope and with notice."

Redline language snippets (draft):
- Liability cap: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Provider's aggregate liability for all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the total Fees paid by Customer to Provider in the twelve (12) months prior to the claim, except to the extent such liability arises from Provider's gross negligence or willful misconduct."

- Data use opt-in: "Provider will not use Customer Data to train or improve Provider's models without the Customer's prior written consent. Provider may use aggregated and anonymized telemetry that cannot reasonably be traced to Customer or an individual for service improvements."

- Security notification: "Provider will provide Customer with initial notice of a security incident affecting Customer Data within forty-eight (48) hours of discovery and will provide regular updates until remediation."

- Indemnity scope: "Provider will indemnify Customer against third-party claims to the extent arising from Provider's breach of its obligations or infringement of third-party IP resulting from Provider's services as authorized under this Agreement. Customer shall indemnify Provider for claims arising from Customer Data or Customer's misuse of the Services."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm finance-approved liability cap number (___).
- For Private deployments: need to confirm whether we can accept any training carve-outs (customer wants model weights access in some cases). Check with product/infra.
- Confirm retention timelines for logs (legal/privacy input).
- Draft fallback SLA credit calculation example to include in annex.

Related artifacts / refs:
- CONFLUENCE-LEGAL-3012 (redline playbook)
- JIRA-CC-8791 (Customer H contract request)
- Slack thread: #legal-sales-thread (link above)

Notes to self:
- Keep this informal — handoff to legal for cleaned up redline.
- Bring up model training prohibition for Private deployments as a selling point to privacy-sensitive customers.
- If customer insists on broader indemnity for outputs, escalate to head of revenue for deal-specific approval.

End of scratchpad.
